sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- IRGC Navy statement, Fri Nov 6] Two oil tankers caught fire after striking mines while attempting to transit via 'unauthorized routes' -- one east of the Strait of Hormuz, one inside it; both had deactivated all navigation and identification systems and were attempting to exit the Strait with US military support; 'The Strait of Hormuz has been closed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy. Nothing will change until Iran's seven conditions are met.' [VERIFIED FACT -- context] A day earlier (Thu Nov 5) Iran claimed five tankers and a tugboat caught fire in similar incidents; UKMTO logged a tanker struck by two unidentified projectiles ~50nm north of Qatar Wed 23:20 UTC (UKMTO 196-26); JMIC 111 counted 4 attacks in Hormuz Nov 1-3. [COUNTED, STALE] IMF PortWatch counted 4 transits through Hormuz on 2026-10-18, 7-day avg 3.7 vs 2025 baseline 85.5/day -- STALE (latest observation Oct 18, snapshot portwatch-2026-10-26.json). [COUNTED, JMIC] ~31 US-assisted transits/day (JMIC 111, Nov 5) vs 34/day Oct 24-30 average. [COUNTED, UNTIERED TRACKER] hormuz.now AIS count: 9 crossings on Nov 5, 7-day avg 9.0/day (~11% of normal, baseline 84.8/day), as of Nov 6 08:27 UTC -- no declared tier, reported with attribution only.
sections.what_verified: IRGC statement carried by Al Arabiya (T3, STATE SA) and Arab News (T3, published 08:13:45Z = 12:13 , in-window). Geneva Times, Shafaq and LaPresse carry the same statement but have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count toward corroboration. The STATEMENT is confirmed; the EVENT (tankers actually hit mines) is UNVERIFIED -- no vessel names, nationalities, casualties, or independent confirmation; Arab News: 'no confirmation of any of these incidents from maritime officials.'
sections.what_disputed: UKMTO's international incident record lists far fewer incidents than Iran's claims (SNN Finland: the regional body logged only one strike on Tuesday off Oman); Gulf News: 'it remains unclear whether any of the reported incidents overlap' -- Friday's two tankers may be the same vessels as Thursday's claims; SOFX: open-source trackers could confirm only the Grit (hit NE of Lima, Oman, Iraqi crude, Barbados-flagged) and the Era S. bulk carrier (Nov 2); no independent confirmation of mines, damage or casualties.
sections.why_matters: Two more tankers ablaze? The IRGC's Friday claim -- two tankers hit mines -- with the verification gap in the headline: no names, no independent confirmation, and a counted-transit reality of ~9 crossings a day.

totw_analysis: Our read: Two more tankers ablaze? The IRGC's Friday claim -- two tankers hit mines -- with the verification gap in the headline: no names, no independent confirmation, and a counted-transit reality of ~9 crossings a day. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Only the IRGC is reporting this -- are tankers really burning, or is Tehran running a mine-claims campaign to keep the strait closed while talks continue? Comment threads split on IRGC credibility vs US-blockade blame (Reuters FB: 360 likes / 35 comments, polarized; Roya News FB: 750 likes / 60 comments).
